title: Complementary sample preparation strategies (PVD/BEXP) combining with multifunctional SPM for the characterizations of battery interfacial properties
author: Pan, Chen, et al.

steps.title: Deposit CuO anode by PVD
steps.instruction: Using conventional physical vapor deposition (PVD) target preparation and deposition procedures, deposit a thin‑film CuO anode onto a polished stainless‑steel substrate, which provides an electrochemically inert current collector without a surface oxidation layer.

steps.title: Deposit LiCoO₂ cathode by PVD
steps.instruction: Using the same PVD approach, deposit a thin‑film LiCoO₂ cathode onto an alumina substrate (or alternatively onto a polished stainless‑steel substrate if desired) for subsequent in‑situ SPM characterization.

steps.title: Cut composite electrode by BEXP
steps.instruction: Prepare composite electrode sections with the beam‑exit polishing (BEXP) method: orient the sample at a tilt angle relative to the Ar‑ion beam so that the ion‑polished surface forms an extended low‑angle slope rather than a steep cross‑section, yielding a large, contamination‑free area suitable for horizontal mounting on a conductive substrate for simultaneous electrochemistry and in‑situ SPM measurements.

steps.title: Assemble in‑situ EC cell
steps.instruction: In an Ar‑filled glove box with moisture and oxygen below 0.1 ppm, assemble the electrochemical cell using the listed components and follow the ordered actions.

substeps.instruction: Place the working electrode (WE) under investigation on the top of the nickel‑plated tungsten alloy base, make electrical contact, and secure it between the base and the 2205 stainless‑steel ring using four flat‑head screws.

Insert the PTFE (Teflon®) insulating insert into the cell body, then position the counter electrode (CE) and reference electrode (RE – Ag/AgCl, Li or Na metal) strips on top of the insulator without touching the WE or the cell body.
Fit the laser‑cut fused silica “glass” cover onto the top of the cell and tighten the retaining screws, completing the mechanical assembly.
Through the hole in the glass cover, add a suitable amount of electrolyte so that the WE, RE, and CE are fully saturated; this ensures the cell is ready for measurements.
